test.name: Generic how-to research question should route to search-familysearch-wiki
test.description: User asks a generic 'how do I find [record type]' research-method/how-to question with no specific place to survey. That is search-familysearch-wiki's territory (research methods via the FamilySearch Research Wiki), not locality-guide's. locality-guide surveys what records exist for a SPECIFIC place and where they are held; it must not grab a generic how-to question. Reciprocal of the search-familysearch-wiki side (ut_search_wiki_003 positive how-to; ut_search_wiki_005 negative that routes a place records-availability survey to locality-guide) — the two skills' descriptions each carry a DO NOT clause pointing at the other.

input.user_message: How do I find marriage records for my ancestors?

negative.explanation: A generic 'how do I find [record type]' question is a research-method/how-to question, which search-familysearch-wiki handles via the FamilySearch Research Wiki. locality-guide produces a records-availability survey for a SPECIFIC place (what exists, where held) and must not grab a general how-to question that names no place to survey. This is the locality-guide side of the search-familysearch-wiki-vs-locality-guide separation: locality-guide's description now carries a DO NOT clause routing generic how-to questions to search-familysearch-wiki.
